paras: The expulsion of Black renters from the Tomberlin neighborhood took place in Lonoke County, Arkansas, in January 1903, when night riders notified every Black renter on lands there to leave at once. The Newport Independent reported that thirty-five families moved away, and Arkansas papers explained the notices as a dispute over rising farm rents.

According to the Newport Independent, landowners in the area had recently raised rents from $4 and $5 to $6 and $7, a rise that a shorter brief specified was per acre. The paper said the increase "antagonized the white renters," whose sympathizers proposed "to reduce rentals by causing shortage of renters." Both versions presented this cause as a supposition rather than an established fact.

During the week before 22 January 1903, "nightriders" notified all Black renters on lands in the Tomberlin neighborhood to leave the country at once. As a result, the Newport Independent said, thirty-five families "moved to more congenial districts." No names of the families or of the night riders appear in the coverage, and no violence beyond the notices was reported.
No report of arrests, an investigation or any official response was found.

The Newport Independent ran the fullest account on 22 January under the headline "Negro Renters Terrorized," calling the episode an "expulsion," and its weekly edition repeated the text the next day. A shorter brief headed "Warned to Leave," opening with "It is said," appeared in the Forrest City Times on 23 January. The same brief was then reprinted in columns of Arkansas news in Malvern, Magnolia and De Queen papers between 28 and 30 January.
None of the white papers commented on the night riders or called for action, treating the episode as a rent quarrel among renters. No Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

The two versions differ on place and outcome: the Newport Independent placed the notices in the Tomberlin neighborhood of Lonoke County and said thirty-five families had moved, while the "Warned to Leave" brief spoke of "a number of negro tenants near England" warned by "unknown men," of whom "many are preparing to comply." Their identical rent figures and shared phrasing suggest a single episode reported twice, though neither text links the two place names.

accounts.label: Newport Independent report
accounts.gist: Nightriders notified all Black renters in the Tomberlin neighborhood, Lonoke county, to leave at once, and 35 families moved; white renters and their sympathizers, angered by rent increases, were said to want a shortage of renters.

accounts.label: 'Warned to Leave' state brief
accounts.gist: Unknown men notified a number of Black tenants near England to leave the county, and many were preparing to comply; the rent increase was the supposed cause.

framing.detail: The Newport Independent headlined it 'Negro Renters Terrorized' and called it an 'expulsion', explaining it as a rent dispute among white renters without comment (A1).
The shorter 'Warned to Leave' brief hedged with 'It is said' and ran in boilerplate columns of Arkansas news (A2, A4, A5, A6).

conflicts.note: The two texts share the rent figures and wording and probably describe the same episode, but neither links the two place names.
A1 reports a completed departure with a number; A2 reports only preparations; the coverage does not settle which is more current.
Not a contradiction so much as different wording; neither names anyone.
